hardest: Let the rest fall away, and only that steadiness remains
why: It is unclear whether this still describes the stone or tells the person to drop something, and "the rest" never says what should fall away, so the image never plainly connects to the person's own life.
last: It says Tiwaz is the name of this stone, one that keeps pointing the right way while everything around it changes.

hardest: the stone changed by water that never asked which way to go
why: The phrase doesn't make clear whether the water or the stone "never asked", and nothing links being carried by a river to the closing question about giving things away, so the reader has to guess at the connection.
last: It asks what you have given away without thinking about the cost, and whether you would do it again.

hardest: What you know does not stay whole until it is handed over
why: "Does not stay whole until" is a twisted way of saying your knowledge is only complete once you share it, so a reader has to stop and untangle it.
last: It asks you to think about who in your life has been waiting for something that only you can give them.

hardest: What one hand gives here, Kuky, still waits in the other.
why: "Hand" could mean a clock hand or a person's hand, so the reader can't tell whether the gift was received or is still being held back.
last: It says that something one person offered has not yet been received or answered by the other and is still waiting.

hardest: What ripens slowly ripens for others as much as for you.
why: It suddenly brings in unnamed "others" and never says who they are or what that means for Kuky.
last: The last sentence says that something that ripens slowly benefits other people as well as Kuky.

why: The reading never explains the name Hagalaz, but the imagery makes clear it is a disruptive force, so the message still comes through.
last: It tells the person to make their decision based on what is still solid and reliable, not on what is already shifting or falling apart.

why: A reader who knows nothing about runes won't know Raidho is a rune's name, but the cairn picture still gets the meaning across.
last: It asks whether you focus on what is right in front of you or on the faint next step ahead.

hardest: whatever comes to take from your hand and leave something in return
why: The reading never says who or what "comes", so the closing exchange stays a riddle rather than something the reader can apply.
last: It says you stand at the point where your old foundations meet something new that will take from you and give something back.

hardest: When the making itself carries its own light
why: The reading never says what "the making" or "the work" is, and the question about whose hands to have beside you comes with no lead-up.
last: It asks who you want working next to you, now that the work keeps itself going.

hardest: the water carrying things toward you before they reach the surface
why: A reader can't tell what "things" are coming or what "reaching the surface" would mean in their own life.
last: It asks Kuky whether to wait until the situation becomes clear or to act now while it is still murky and strong.

hardest: the water keeps its own pace beside it
why: The reading never says what the river stands for, so a reader can't tell whether it is a companion, time, or just scenery.
last: It says this path was never only yours: others share it, or walk it with you.

hardest: the last heat is already leaving, unseen
why: The reader can't tell whether the cooling coffee means something is being lost, which would suggest hurrying, or just that time is passing quietly, and the next sentence says to wait.
last: It says that whatever patience or attention you put into waiting will quietly come back to you.
